Consult Summary:
- Telehealth consult for patient with 1-week history of fever with sweats, chills, myalgias, and nausea after recent travel to Vietnam; no localizing symptoms identified; plan for urgent in-person assessment and blood tests including malaria screening.

History:
- Presenting complaint: Fever for ~7 days with alternating hot/cold episodes, night sweats, diffuse myalgias, nausea, fatigue; poor appetite and low oral intake (drinking small amounts).
- Timeline: Symptoms began ~7 days ago; persistent; minimal transient relief with OTC antipyretics.
- Modifying factors: Ibuprofen and paracetamol at recommended doses provide slight, temporary benefit.
- Associated symptoms:
  - Positive: Night sweats, chills, diffuse muscle aches, nausea, fatigue.
  - Negative: No cough, sore throat, ear pain, diarrhea, neck stiffness, rash, swollen/tender joints (chronic back pain baseline only), dysuria, urinary frequency/urgency.
  - Headache: Not worse than usual; chronic, centralized; historically associated with screen use and weather changes. Conflict noted regarding migraines (see Quality checks).
- Recent travel: Returned from Vietnam 4 weeks ago; rural and urban exposure; trekking and cycling through farmland; took daily malaria prophylaxis (names not recalled); possibly combination regimen (patient unsure).

Past Medical History:
- Chronic back pain related to prolonged sitting/poor posture; under active physiotherapy management.
- Headaches; patient later states sometimes has migraines triggered by weather; initial statement denied migraines (conflict noted).

Medications:
- Seroxat (paroxetine) — dose/route/frequency not documented.
- Ibuprofen (OTC) — dose/route/frequency not documented; reported taken at “recommended dose.”
- Paracetamol (acetaminophen) (OTC) — dose/route/frequency not documented; reported taken at “recommended dose.”
- Recent malaria chemoprophylaxis during travel — specific agents not recalled; regimen details not documented.

Allergies:
- Pollen (hay fever).
- No medication allergies reported.

Social History:
- Occupation: Nurse; reports difficulty working due to fatigue.
- Immunizations: Up to date, including Hepatitis B (occupational).
- Tobacco: Non-smoker.
- Alcohol: Moderate intake.
- Exercise: Moderate exercise a few times per week.
- Travel: Vietnam (returned 4 weeks ago); rural/urban exposure; trekking/cycling.

Family History:
- Father: Myocardial infarction; deceased at approximately age 68.

Physical Examination:
- Not performed (telehealth). No vitals documented.

Investigations:
- Planned:
  - Thick and thin blood films for malaria.
  - Inflammatory markers (e.g., CRP/ESR) — specific tests not itemized.
  - Additional blood tests to identify source of infection (details not specified).
- No results available.

Assessment & Plan:
- Issue 1: Febrile illness with night sweats and myalgias, 1-week duration, no clear localizing source on history.
  - Plan:
    - Urgent in-person clinical examination at central London clinic (same-day if possible); alternative option: attend local A&E if clinic attendance is inconvenient.
    - Order blood tests including inflammatory markers and other labs as per examining clinician.
    - Work exclusion advised until evaluation completed and safe to return.
- Issue 2: Recent travel to Vietnam with rural exposure; malaria risk despite prophylaxis.
  - Plan:
    - Order thick and thin blood films for malaria.
    - Consider other exotic/travel-related infections per examining clinician’s assessment; urgency of testing to be guided by in-person findings.
- Issue 3: Chronic back pain related to posture; under physiotherapy.
  - Plan:
    - No changes discussed during this consult.

- General Plan items:
  - Admin team to arrange clinic appointment; patient to call provided number to be scheduled and present consult note at reception.
  - Clinician will document testing requests and rationale in the notes for receiving team.

Quality checks:
- Missing expected elements: No vitals, no physical exam findings, no laboratory data, incomplete medication details (doses/routes/frequencies not documented), pregnancy status not discussed, COVID-19 or flu exposure/testing not discussed, hydration status guidance not provided.
- Internal conflicts: Patient initially denied migraines (“No migraines”), later reported sometimes struggling with migraines related to weather; conflict noted.
- Transcript quality: Minor gaps/inaudible segments and brief clinician misspeaks; overall history adequate for triage and planning.
